title: Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme (HKPFS)
description: Established by the Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong in 2009, the Hong Kong PhD Fellowship Scheme aims at attracting the best and brightest students in the world to pursue their PhD studies in Hong Kong's universities. Fellows receive an annual stipend plus a conference and research-related travel allowance, and study at one of the UGC-funded universities with full tuition fee remission for the normative study period.
official_source: Research Grants Council of Hong Kong
eligibility: Full-time PhD students who are studying in any of the UGC-funded universities
All applicants, regardless of ethnicity, nationality, prior work experience and ethnic background, should be eligible to apply
New students who are admitted for a PhD in the UGC-funded universities for 2026/27
eligibility_summary: Open to students of any nationality admitted to a full-time PhD at a UGC-funded university in Hong Kong for the 2026/27 academic year.
benefits: Conference and research-related travel allowance of HK$14,400 (approximately US$1,850) for the 2026/27 academic year
Tuition fee remission for the normative study period
requirements: Admission to a full-time PhD programme at a UGC-funded university
documents: PhD admission application via the university
Application for HKPFS via the university
application_method: Apply for PhD admission to a UGC-funded university and indicate interest in HKPFS
Fellowship applications are submitted through the university
selection_notes: Shortlisted applications are reviewed by one of two Selection Panels comprising experts in the relevant board areas.
best_fit: Top PhD applicants worldwide who want to pursue doctoral research in Hong Kong.
notes: The fellowship is awarded for the normative study period. Amounts published for the 2026/27 academic year.

verification.notes: Stipend and travel allowance figures confirmed on the RGC HKPFS page for the 2026/27 academic year. Exact application deadline is set by each UGC-funded university; 1 December 2026 is the typical main-round deadline.

title: Rhodes Scholarship (University of Oxford)
description: The Rhodes Scholarship is a fully-funded postgraduate award which enables talented people from around the world to study full-time at the University of Oxford. Rhodes Scholars come to the UK for two or more years and can apply to study most full-time postgraduate courses in almost any field offered by Oxford University.
duration: Two or more years (depends on course and degree combination)
application_period: Applications for the current cycle are closed; next cycle opens in 2026
eligibility: Citizenship of an eligible Rhodes constituency
Age eligibility limits apply by constituency
Completion of an undergraduate degree before taking up the Scholarship
eligibility_summary: Citizens or residents of an eligible Rhodes constituency worldwide, within the constituency age limits, with a completed undergraduate degree.
benefits: All University of Oxford course fees
Annual stipend of £20,400 per annum (£1,700 per month) for the 2025-26 academic year
Settling in allowance on arrival in Oxford
The application fee required to apply to Oxford
Assistance to cover visa fees when transitioning to a second course of study
requirements: Eligibility for a full-time postgraduate course at Oxford
english_requirement: Oxford's standard English language requirements apply
application_method: Apply online via the Rhodes Trust application portal for your constituency
Candidates must secure endorsement from their university
selection_notes: The Scholarship is merit-based, with the purpose of developing public-spirited leaders and promoting international understanding and peace.
best_fit: Outstanding future leaders with academic excellence and public service commitment.
notes: Stipend figure published for the 2025-26 academic year (£20,400 per annum). Applications for the current cycle are closed; the next cycle is expected to open in 2026.

verification.notes: Fully-funded status, stipend amount (£20,400 for 2025-26) and coverage confirmed on the Rhodes Trust page. The exact opening date for the next application cycle was not published at time of research.

title: Churchill Scholarship
description: The Churchill Scholarship funds one year of master's study at the University of Cambridge for US citizens pursuing graduate study in science, technology, engineering and mathematics. It is a transformational programme in Cambridge's research-intensive science environment.
official_source: Winston Churchill Foundation of the United States
eligibility: US citizenship
Completion of a bachelor's degree by the time the Scholarship begins
Outstanding academic achievement in STEM
eligibility_summary: US citizens with a bachelor's degree and exceptional academic record who intend to pursue a one-year master's programme in STEM at the University of Cambridge.
benefits: Full tuition at the University of Cambridge
requirements: Admission to an eligible one-year master's programme at Cambridge
Nomination by a participating US college or university
application_method: Applicants must be nominated by their US institution
Nomination deadline is 2 November 2026 at 5pm Eastern
Nominated applicants then complete the Churchill application
selection_notes: Selection is by the Churchill Foundation with Cambridge input on eligible programmes.
best_fit: High-achieving US graduates pursuing STEM master's study at Cambridge.
notes: The official site states the 2026 application is open with a nomination deadline of 2 November 2026. The scholarship covers the eligible one-year Cambridge master's programmes listed on the site.

verification.notes: Open status, nomination deadline (2 November 2026) and fully-funded nature confirmed on the official site. Exact stipend value is not published in monetary terms on the site.

title: University of Southern California (USC) Merit Scholarships
description: USC awards merit scholarships to help undergraduate students pay for their education. Merit scholarships are reserved for students with special qualifications, such as academic, athletic or artistic talent, and are administered through the Office of Admission. Awards range in value from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition.
official_source: University of Southern California, Office of Admission
eligibility: Incoming undergraduate applicants
Students with academic, athletic or artistic talent
Students do not need to submit a need-based financial aid application to be considered for a merit scholarship
eligibility_summary: Incoming undergraduate students demonstrating academic, athletic or artistic excellence, considered automatically through the admission application.
benefits: Awards ranging from a few thousand dollars up to full tuition
A scholarship valued at $20,000 per year for students named National Merit Finalists by the National Merit Corporation who list USC as first-choice
Departmental and alumni group awards varying from a few thousand dollars to upwards of $10,000
application_method: Apply for undergraduate admission to USC; no separate scholarship application required for Office of Admission merit scholarships
Some departmental and alumni awards require separate applications
selection_notes: Merit scholarships are awarded based on academic excellence, leadership, service and other special qualifications. Need-based financial aid is a separate process.
best_fit: Talented undergraduate applicants to USC seeking merit-based funding without a separate need-based aid application.
notes: Application deadlines for USC Merit Scholarships follow the USC first-year application deadlines published on the admission site.

logo.image_alt_text: University of Southern California, Office of Admission

verification.notes: Award range (a few thousand to full tuition), the $20,000/year National Merit Finalist award and the separate need-based process confirmed on the official page. Specific deadlines are on the USC Dates and Deadlines page.

title: Stanford University Need-Based Financial Aid (International Applicants)
description: Stanford University operates a need-based financial aid program for undergraduate students. Stanford meets the full demonstrated need of eligible students without expecting them to borrow. The average scholarship and grant from all sources received by need-based aid recipients in the current freshman class is $74,310, including an average Stanford scholarship of $66,259.
eligibility: Undergraduate applicants with demonstrated financial need
Aid eligibility is determined by family financial circumstances, family size, number of family members in college and family assets
eligibility_summary: Undergraduate applicants who demonstrate financial need; Stanford meets full demonstrated need without loans for eligible students.
benefits: Average scholarship and grant from all sources of $74,310 for the current freshman class
Stanford meets full demonstrated need without expecting eligible students to borrow
coverage: Tuition, mandatory fees, room and board (gift aid portion)
requirements: Submission of Stanford's financial aid application
application_method: Apply for undergraduate admission
Submit Stanford's financial aid application by the published deadline
selection_notes: Aid is need-based. Athletes may receive additional Pell Grant or athletic aid on top.
best_fit: International undergraduate applicants to Stanford with strong financial need.
notes: The average figures published are for the current freshman class (Class of 2028). Stanford notes that only a small portion of aid recipients receive federal data based aid because Stanford meets need without loans.

verification.notes: Average aid figures ($74,310 total, $66,259 Stanford scholarship) and the need-based, no-loan policy confirmed on the official Stanford financial aid page. Award amounts vary by family circumstance.

title: Kyoto University International Undergraduate Program (Kyoto iUP)
description: Kyoto iUP is a 4.5-year English-taught bachelor's degree programme at Kyoto University for students with no prior Japanese language proficiency. Students receive a preparatory Japanese language course followed by degree study, and upon graduation are awarded a bachelor's degree in their selected major. Financial support includes admission and tuition fee waivers and monthly scholarships.
duration: 4.5 years (6 months Japanese language + 4 years degree)
application_period: October 2027 enrollment; new application guidelines available
eligibility: Students with no prior Japanese language education
Completion of 12 years of school education
Application for October 2027 enrollment
eligibility_summary: Students who have completed 12 years of schooling and have no prior Japanese language education, applying for October 2027 enrollment.
benefits: Bachelor's degree awarded in the selected major on graduation
requirements: Required application documents per the published guidelines
english_requirement: The programme is taught in English; no prior Japanese language education is required
application_method: Submit an application through the official Kyoto iUP admissions process
New application guidelines for October 2027 enrollment are published on the programme site
selection_notes: Selection includes a document screening process run by Kyoto University.
program_type: English-taught bachelor's degree programme with scholarship support
best_fit: International students who want an English-taught bachelor's degree in Japan and to learn Japanese from beginner level.
notes: The programme site states that new application guidelines for October 2027 enrollment are now available. Exact deadline and stipend amounts are published in the detailed guidelines.

verification.notes: Programme structure (4.5 years, English-taught, no prior Japanese required), fee waivers and monthly scholarships confirmed on the official Kyoto iUP site. The October 2027 application deadline and exact monthly stipend amount are in the detailed guidelines document, not on the landing page.

title: University of Birmingham Postgraduate Chancellor's Scholarships
description: The University of Birmingham offers Postgraduate Chancellor's Scholarships for international students pursuing a full-time postgraduate master's programme starting in September 2026. Awards are worth £10,000 towards tuition fees (first year only) and are offered by country, including China, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Thailand, Türkiye, Vietnam, Nigeria, Ghana and Kenya.

eligibility: International students from the eligible country lists (China, India, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Thailand, Türkiye, Vietnam, Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Europe and others)
Enrolment on a full-time postgraduate master's programme starting September 2026
Students are automatically considered where applicable
eligibility_summary: International students from eligible countries starting a full-time postgraduate master's programme at Birmingham in September 2026.
benefits: More than £10 million in scholarships available for international students at Birmingham
requirements: Admission to a full-time postgraduate master's programme starting September 2026
application_method: Apply for the relevant postgraduate master's programme; applicants are considered automatically where applicable
selection_notes: Scholarships celebrate outstanding achievement and recognise talent from around the world. Awards are subject to the University's international scholarship terms and conditions.
best_fit: International master's applicants to the University of Birmingham from eligible countries.
notes: Awards are first-year only. The University also offers a £5,000 Postgraduate High Fliers Scholarship and a Future Skills Scholarship of up to £12,500 for Indian students.

verification.notes: £10,000 first-year tuition award, September 2026 start, eligible country lists and the £5,000 High Fliers and £12,500 Future Skills amounts confirmed on the official Birmingham page. Deadlines are on individual scholarship pages.

The programme brings together future leaders from around the world.

English language proficiency

title: McGill University Entrance Scholarships
description: McGill University offers centrally-administered merit-based entrance scholarships for first-year undergraduate students. One-year entrance scholarships are valued at $3,000 (non-renewable), while Major Entrance Scholarships are valued between $12,000 and $48,000 ($3,000 to $12,000 per annum, renewable for up to 4 years).
duration: One year, or renewable for up to 4 years (major awards)
official_source: McGill University, Scholarships and Student Aid
eligibility: First-year undergraduate applicants to McGill
Transfer, Mature, Diploma, Exchange, Special, Part-time and Visiting students are not eligible
Awarded solely on the basis of academic achievement
eligibility_summary: New first-year undergraduate students admitted to McGill who meet the minimum academic requirements for an entrance scholarship.
benefits: Major Entrance Scholarships valued between $12,000 and $48,000 ($3,000 to $12,000 per annum renewable for up to 4 years, provided academic standing is maintained)
requirements: Admission to a McGill first-year undergraduate programme
application_method: Apply for admission to McGill
Applicants to eligible programmes get access to the Major Entrance Scholarship application
selection_notes: Entrance scholarships are awarded solely on the basis of academic achievement. Meeting the minimum requirements does not guarantee an offer. The $12,000 level is only available to Canadian citizens or legal permanent residents of Canada.
best_fit: High-achieving first-year undergraduate applicants to McGill.
notes: McGill notes an eligibility update effective Fall 2026 for certain programmes. Awards are renewable subject to academic standing for major awards.

verification.notes: Award values ($3,000 one-year; $12,000-48,000 major), eligibility rules and the Canadian citizen/permanent resident restriction on the $12,000 level confirmed on the official McGill page.

description: VLIR-UOS awards ICP Connect study scholarships to applicants from 28 eligible countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America to attend accredited international study programmes taught in English at Flemish universities or universities of applied sciences and arts. Scholarships cover tuition fees, travel, insurance and living expenses for the full duration of the study programme.

duration: Full duration of the study programme (12/24/36 months)
eligibility: Nationality from one of the 28 eligible countries and residence in one of those countries at the time of application
Age: not older than 35 (bachelor or initial master) or 45 (advanced master) as of 1 January of the intake year; bachelor applicants must be at least 19
One ICP Connect scholarship application per year; no other concurrent scholarship or grant
No previous Belgian government study scholarship and no prior enrolment at a Belgian higher education institution before 1 January of the intake year
eligibility_summary: Candidates from the 28 eligible countries in Africa, Asia and Latin America within the age limits, applying to an ICP Connect study programme.
benefits: Scholarship awarded for the full duration of the study programme (12/24/36 months)
requirements: Admission to an ICP Connect study programme at a Flemish university
documents: Scholarship application via the institution's website
english_requirement: The study programmes are taught in English
application_method: Apply for both the programme and the scholarship through the institution's website
Indicate interest in the scholarship when submitting the programme application
selection_notes: Scholars are evaluated on motivation and professional goals as potential agents of change, professional experience, academic results and commitment to sustainable development. Female candidates are strongly encouraged; a gender balance is targeted.
best_fit: Students and professionals from the 28 eligible partner countries pursuing an English-taught master's in Belgium.
notes: The 2026-2027 call is closed; the 2027-2028 call is expected to open by the end of October 2026 with programme-specific deadlines. Scholarship costs may change in line with government funding decisions.

verification.notes: Coverage (tuition, travel, insurance, living expenses), eligibility rules and the 2027-2028 call timing confirmed on the official VLIR-UOS page. Exact scholarship amounts are set in the current scholarship framework, which was not loaded.
